known_issues: The caller authenticates independently expected packet/context/profile identities. Kernel seals and completed inspection do not authenticate the sender or authorize report release.

Capture uses immutable bytes and preserves the borrowed descriptor and offset. The descriptor is not retained or reread after capture. Caller-owned duplicates and hostile concurrent descriptor-table manipulation remain outside this contract.

Only the unchanged snapshot job performs complete source/PDF admission and existing guarded native inspection. No caller-selected executor, override, precomputed result, retry, service, socket or stored job queue is introduced.

The exact existing result is returned with its existing resource profile and all qualification flags. No wrapper converts unsigned observations into authenticated execution or scientific, reading-order, PDF-UA, finding-completeness or release certification.
The original job acceptance clock starts inside its existing flow. It does not impose hard total time, aggregate CPU/memory/scratch/process limits or descendant cleanup on this outer call.

Packet capture and bounded result checking add finite copying and JSON-decoding overhead; these are not zero-copy or total resource qualification. Plaintext handling, swap and authorized private delivery remain outer-boundary responsibilities.
Original 32-page/8-MiB default rendering and optional 64-page/8-MiB inspection remain unchanged. No long-report delivery or larger PDF profile is activated.
